people.lifeDatesNote: The Encyclopédie multimédia de la comédie musicale théâtrale en France gives 15 May 1878 as the birth date, whereas GND gives 18 August 1888. Both give 21 January 1942 as the death date. The displayed dates follow 1878–1942; the birth-date discrepancy remains unresolved.

sources.researchNote: The page gives the civil-status name Amédée Ferdinand Pujol and the dates Bordeaux, 15 May 1878 – Paris, 21 January 1942, together with a list of stage works and press articles. The birth year conflicts across authority sources: the Library of Congress record no2009029783 gives 1888 and GND 1062158474 gives 18 August 1888, while VIAF 44567556 and this encyclopedia give 1878, the latter with the precise date 15 May. All sources agree on the death date, 21 January 1942. The preferred birth year is 1878; the discrepancy remains unresolved.

media.title: René Pujol — portrait by Henri Manuel, 1932
media.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of René Pujol in profile, wearing a suit.
media.publicCaption: René Pujol, the Bordeaux-born librettist who wrote with Charles-Louis Pothier under Albert Willemetz at the Bouffes-Parisiens, photographed by Henri Manuel for the programme of La Pouponnière.
media.publicCreditLine: Henri Manuel (1874–1947); programme of La Pouponnière, Bouffes-Parisiens, 1932, collection Jacques Gana, via the Encyclopédie de la comédie musicale.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photographer, Henri Manuel, died in 1947, so the French term expired on 1 January 2018; because the work was still protected in France on the URAA date of 1 January 1996, United States copyright was restored and runs ninety-five years from the 1932 publication, to 1 January 2028. The site that reproduces the programme grants no licence, stating that illustrations remain the copyright of their respective rightsholders. A reduced-resolution reproduction (700 × 852 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
